title: swing-shift-scratchpad-oncall-playbook
content:
Purpose: quick personal playbook for swing shift (1600-0000 PT). Not official runbook, this is my working notes to help triage/disambiguate noisy alerts. Keep short, add to shared runbook when stable.

Shift start checklist:
- Read last handoff notes (search Slack thread: #oncall-handoffs).
- Open Grafana: inference-overview, model-latency, shard-utilization.
- Pager status: ensure Ops Pager is routed to my mobile.
- Run quick healthcheck: curl -sS https://health.redwood.internal/v1/health | jq .
- Note any active incidents in Jira/Slack and summarize in Handoff line: status / active alerts / mitigation in-place.

Triage flow (fast):
1) Identify symptom: high latency / error spike / OOM / 5xx ratio / queue backlog.
2) Reproduce on a small scale: run sample request with same route and model tag, include same headers.
3) Check dashboards:
   - p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec (Grafana link above)
   - GPU util by node (node-exporter + nvml)
   - Queue depth / batch sizes (serving runtime metrics)
   - KV cache hit ratio and redis evictions
4) Tail logs (only if needed): kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime --tail=200 | rg "ERROR|OOM|timeout"

Common quick fixes (do first, low blast radius):
- If single node OOM: cordon + drain pod, let HPA re-create. kubectl cordon <node> then evict pods.
- If model variant causing latency regressions: switch to fallback variant via Console -> Routes -> Edit -> Fallback model (or use admin API POST /admin/route/fallback).
- High batch size causing latency: reduce batch target for the route, restart router process if needed.
- Redis/KV failures: check redis-stats, restart single redis replica, check alerts for packet loss.

Escalation matrix:
- If >2% 5xx or p95 > 2x SLO for >10m: escalate to SRE lead Arjun Patel (Slack @arjun) and page infra oncall.
- If model corrupted / release regression suspected: tag research applied-ml and model-oncall channel, open Jira: JIRA-INC-8721.
- For customer-impacting data leakage or security: immediate page Security lead Lina Rodriguez and follow security escalation playbook.

Temporary procedures to add to canonical runbook (items to convert from this scratchpad):
- Precise commands for safe model failover (include admin-token steps).
- Rollback checklist for quantized model releases.
- Minimum telemetry to keep during emergency (metrics to always capture).

Notes to self / unresolved:
- Investigate flaky alert: "inference.request.timeout" wallclock vs token-timeout mismatch. Maybe config drift from router->worker. Add a config check script.
- Script idea: one-liner to snapshot all runtime env vars + pod list for postmortem.

Handoff template (copy into Slack at end):
- status: GREEN / YELLOW / RED
- active incidents: short bullets with JIRA keys
- actions taken: short bullets
- items to follow-up: short bullets (who -> what -> ETA)

Quick snippets I use:
- health: curl -sS https://health.redwood.internal/v1/health | jq .
- tail logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=router --tail=150 -f
- check gpu: ./infra/tools/gpu-util.sh --summary
- fallback API: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.internal/api/v1/routes/route-id/fallback -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-v2"}'

End of scratchpad. Will clean and push to shared runbook once steps are validated on next handoff.
